heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles Elegoo Rapid PETG natively without enclosure or nozzle hardware upgrades, reaching print speeds up to 238 mm/s backed by a 20 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate. Excellent thermal stability and direct-drive extrusion allow this open-frame setup to deliver functional PETG parts quickly and reliably.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent to prevent surface damage
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 20 mm³/s in the filament settings to safely sustain printing up to 238 mm/s without underextrusion.
Configure Nozzle Temperature to 245°C for initial and subsequent layers, and set Bed Temperature to 78°C to ensure solid bed adhesion.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' with a 2 mm wipe distance to minimize PETG oozing and fine stringing during high-speed travel moves.
Set Pressure Advance (PA) to 0.038 using linear advance calibration to eliminate corner swelling at elevated speeds.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine cobwebs between travel moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG has absorbed ambient moisture, lowering melt viscosity and causing high-temperature oozing.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours in a filament dryer, and increase retraction speed to 40 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Print tearing chunks out of the PEI coating on part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG bonds chemically to PEI when printed directly on clean, bare textured or smooth plates.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin layer of PVA glue stick or Bambu liquid glue as an interface release agent before printing, and let the bed cool fully to room temperature before part removal.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer delamination or poor structural part strength
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speed preventing adequate polymer chain fusion between layers at high speeds.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower maximum part cooling fan speed to 40% and increase hotend temperature to 250°C to maximize layer adhesion.

faq.question: Does the Bambu Lab A1 need an enclosure to print Elegoo Rapid PETG?
faq.answer: No, Elegoo Rapid PETG prints reliably on the open-frame Bambu Lab A1 without an enclosure because PETG does not suffer from high shrinkage or extreme thermal draft sensitivity like ABS or ASA.

faq.question: Can the stock stainless steel nozzle on the A1 handle Elegoo Rapid PETG?
faq.answer: Yes, standard Elegoo Rapid PETG is completely non-abrasive, making the stock stainless steel 0.4mm nozzle fully sufficient for long-term production.

faq.question: Why is glue stick recommended if the Bambu textured PEI plate provides good adhesion?
faq.answer: PETG adheres excessively well to PEI coatings, posing a risk of ripping the PEI film off the steel spring sheet upon removal. Glue acts as a sacrificial release layer rather than an adhesive.

faq.question: How do I achieve the rated 238 mm/s speed without underextruding?
faq.answer: Set the Max Volumetric Speed in OrcaSlicer to 20 mm³/s and the hotend temperature to 245°C-250°C to guarantee smooth plasticization at high travel rates.
